speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The baskets are roped. The brazier is sinking. These pages have not been tried. I want them heard before I trust them.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Read, then. I am not standing up for a speech. I sat for the last ones.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A tailor. He is given his bill, and he cannot read it, and the rest laugh because a workman is stupid. That is the joke. I wrote it after the play to see if it would stand.

speaker: will_kemp
text: No. Thou'st a tailor there who can't read, and I'll grant thee he can't, but don't make him a fool for it. A man may get a play wrong and want with his whole heart to get it right. That's funnier, and it's kinder, and it's true.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then it does not stand. I am crossing it while thou art in the room, so I do not love it later.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: I have known a joiner who sang bass in the waits for twenty years and never once came in on the beat, and wept at every carol. He was not a fool. He was a man in the wrong bar.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A man who wants it right, and comes in wrong. That I can keep. The laugh was the cheap part.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: If I am to copy what survives, how many of them are there? I do not copy a company that has not been counted.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six. And a lion.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Six men and a skin. Thou wilt not make the skin the wit. The wit is the man who is frightened and goes on.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They will stand in front of a duke with a wall made of a man. That is the labour. There is vanity in it, and a sort of courage. I had the courage the wrong way up.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Let him come in late, and let him weep. Do not give him a speech about the weeping. He will not have one.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: The lines you are crossing. Do you want them copied, or left where the pen goes through?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Left. A fair copy of a bad joke is how a bad joke gets believed. Copy the six, and the lion. Not the tailor's shame.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The weaver still wants every part. That was true on Saturday. Do not punish him for wanting it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not. He may be the lover, and the lady, and the lion, and be loved for the wanting. The ass is not written. I have not written the head.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Then we are hearing a page, and not playing it. My lute is in the case. I brought it in case of a song, and there is no song.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No song. No ending. Field has not heard a word of these pages, and he will not hear this one.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Six. And a lion. I can count that. I cannot count a play that stops in the middle of a joke.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Count six. I am not calling it finished to make the copying easier.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Thou'lt let them be men first. Then make them asses.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Men first. I have crossed the other way. I am not lighting the fire again for a page I do not trust.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: A sinking fire is an honest light. It does not flatter a line. Leave it.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: I will take the sheet when the pen is dry. I have copied a stroke that was still wet, and I will not do it twice.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I am going. Leave them men when I am gone.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Go. The asses can wait. The men are what I have.
